proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap Li-ion insulator with high oxidative stability, so it should block electron transfer at the LiCoO2 surface at 4.0 V. It is also chemically mild toward the sulfide electrolyte, since both share the PO4/PS4 tetrahedral motif and Li-P-based chemistry, which should limit interdiffusion and reactive decomposition. It is a standard protective coating choice, so it is a sensible first probe of the penalty landscape.

LiF is a wide-gap, electrochemically robust Li-ion insulator with very low chemical reactivity toward sulfides. Its fluoride anion is hard and poorly reducing, so the contact with Li6PS5Cl should be thermodynamically mild, unlike the P2O5/SO2 products that drove the Li3PO4 penalty. This tests a halide-family coating rather than another phosphate or oxide.
